title: Seating order on the bandstand and recording
summary: Foster describes where he sat on stands at Economy Hall and Hope's Hall and how the band was placed for the recording.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: One question I was going to ask, how you used to sit on the stand when you'd be on those balconies, you know, like say, at Economy Hall or Hope's Hall. What was the order of the instruments? Where did you sit with your drums? Were you on one end? On the right hand.
On the right hand side and bass on the left hand side.
The bass over on the other hand. Yeah.
And who was next to you? Trombone.
Clarinet. Clarinet. Violin. Guita. Bass. Bass.
When you recorded it, it was a cellar stand band, did you sit in about that order or did they have you sit different?
No, it was set around. Sort of around. Put the drum on the way on the last in the back of the band.
The band would be up front, the drum being the, the drum and the bass being the back.
Yeah. That is done down at the Gottschalk building. Yeah.
Hmm. Gotcha. Right down on the Canal and Chop.
